## Proof

Let $N \sim \mathrm{Poisson}(m)$, so $E[N]=m$ and $\operatorname{Var}(N)=m$. Write $X = N/m$, so that
$$
N + \tfrac{1}{m} = m\Bigl(X + \tfrac{1}{m^{2}}\Bigr),\qquad \log\!\Bigl(N+\tfrac{1}{m}\Bigr) = \log m + \log\!\Bigl(X+\tfrac{1}{m^{2}}\Bigr).
$$
Therefore
$$
\frac{E\!\bigl[\log(N+\tfrac{1}{m})\bigr]}{\log m} = 1 + \frac{E\!\bigl[\log\!\bigl(X+\tfrac{1}{m^{2}}\bigr)\bigr]}{\log m}.
$$
It suffices to show $E\!\bigl[\log\!\bigl(X+\tfrac{1}{m^{2}}\bigr)\bigr] = O(1)$, since then the ratio of the correction with $\log m\to\infty$ vanishes.

**Splitting.** Let $A = \{N \ge m/2\}$ and $B = \{N < m/2\}$.

*On $A$:* $X \ge 1/2$, so $\log\!\bigl(X+\tfrac{1}{m^{2}}\bigr) \ge \log(1/2)$. Also $\log\!\bigl(X+\tfrac{1}{m^{2}}\bigr) \le \log(X+1) \le X$ (using $\log(1+t)\le t$). Hence
$$
\bigl|E\!\bigl[\log\!\bigl(X+\tfrac{1}{m^{2}}\bigr)\mathbf{1}_{A}\bigr]\bigr| \le \max\!\bigl(|\log(1/2)|,\, E[X]\bigr) = \max(\log 2,\,1) = O(1).
$$

*On $B$:* Here $X < 1/2$ and $X + 1/m^{2} \ge 1/m^{2}$ (since $X\ge 0$), so $\log\!\bigl(X+\tfrac{1}{m^{2}}\bigr) \ge -2\log m$, while $\log\!\bigl(X+\tfrac{1}{m^{2}}\bigr) \le \log(1/2) < 0$. Thus
$$
\bigl|E\!\bigl[\log\!\bigl(X+\tfrac{1}{m^{2}}\bigr)\mathbf{1}_{B}\bigr]\bigr| \le 2\log m \cdot P(B).
$$
By the Chernoff bound for Poisson tails, $P(N \le (1-\delta)m) \le \exp\!\bigl(-m\delta^{2}/2\bigr)$; with $\delta = 1/2$,
$$
P(B) = P\!\bigl(N < \tfrac{m}{2}\bigr) \le e^{-m/8}.
$$
Consequently $2\log m \cdot e^{-m/8} = o(1)$.

Combining,
$$
E\!\bigl[\log\!\bigl(X+\tfrac{1}{m^{2}}\bigr)\bigr] = O(1) + o(1) = O(1),
$$
and so
$$
\frac{E\!\bigl[\log\!\bigl(X+\tfrac{1}{m^{2}}\bigr)\bigr]}{\log m} \xrightarrow{m\to\infty} 0.
$$

Therefore
$$
\boxed{\lim_{m\to\infty}\frac{E\!\bigl[\log\!\bigl(N+\tfrac{1}{m}\bigr)\bigr]}{\log m} = 1.}
$$

On $A$: $X \geq 1/2$, $\log(X+1/m^2) \in [\log(1/2), \log(X+1)]$. $|E[\cdot \mathbf{1}_A]| \leq E[|\log(X+1/m^2)|\mathbf{1}_A] \leq \max(|\log(1/2)|, E[\log(X+1)\mathbf{1}_A])$. $\log(X+1) \leq X$, so $\leq E[X] = 1$. So bounded by constant.

On $B$: $N < m/2$. $\log(X+1/m^2) \geq -2\log m$ (since $X+1/m^2 \geq 1/m^2$ when... wait $X = N/m \geq 1/m$ when $N\geq 1$, and $X=0$ when $N=0$ giving $1/m^2$). Lower bound $-2\log m$. Upper bound $\log(1/2 + 1/m^2) \leq \log(1/2) < 0$. So $|E[\cdot\mathbf{1}_B]| \leq 2\log m \cdot P(B)$.

So $E[\log(X+1/m^2)] = O(1) + o(1) = O(1)$. Therefore $\frac{E[\log(X+1/m^2)]}{\log m} \to 0$.
